dataSource: Official Sunnypilot Documentation, release notes, and linked upstream development proposals / issue reports

features.name: M.A.D.S.
features.officialDefinition: Decouples lateral control (steering) from longitudinal control (gas/brake), enabling the car to steer itself even when cruise control is disengaged.
features.userSummary: Steering stays on even if you brake or coast.
features.userTranslation: "Always-On Steering." The car steers for you even if you are in full control of the speed. You can coast, brake, or accelerate without the steering turning off. Brake hold is a separate condition: open PRs #2031 and #2039 propose pause/engagement protection. Ordinary brake-pedal behavior does not guarantee steering remains active during brake hold.

features.name: NNLC
features.officialDefinition: Uses a vehicle-trained neural network to calculate steering commands in place of a conventional lateral controller. It does not replace the driving model or predict its path.
features.userSummary: AI-based steering controller. Note: Mutually exclusive with Enforce Torque Control.
features.userTranslation: Requires a trained model for your vehicle and torque-based steering; angle-steering vehicles are excluded. Configure while parked. NNLC and Enforce Torque Control are mutually exclusive. Issue #2019 reports low-speed oscillation on one Prius Prime/Chestnut setup; that report does not establish a fault on every vehicle.

features.name: Blinker Pause
features.officialDefinition: Pauses steering assist while a turn signal is active below the configured speed threshold. Above that threshold, steering stays active. After the signal turns off, steering resumes following the configured delay.
features.userSummary: Gives back manual steering while your turn signal is blinking.
features.userTranslation: Use the speed threshold and re-engage delay to control when the blinker returns steering to you. This is separate from Auto Lane Change.

features.name: Torque Control
features.officialDefinition: A modern lateral controller that calculates the exact steering motor torque needed based on lateral acceleration, friction, and vehicle dynamics. Features an adaptive self-tuning algorithm that continuously refines steering response in real time.
features.userSummary: Precision torque steering with real-time adaptive self-tuning.
features.userTranslation: "Adaptive Torque Steering." Replaces older steering methods with a high-accuracy torque model. If your car wanders or feels sloppy in curves, turning on Self-Tune lets sunnypilot automatically dial in the steering friction and strength for your specific car.

features.name: DEC
features.officialDefinition: Legacy contextual switching between Chill and Experimental longitudinal modes. PR #2056 removed DEC from master on October 16, 2026; the inspected dev build also omits it, while staging still retains it.
features.userSummary: Legacy mode switching; removed from current master and dev.
features.userTranslation: Check your installed branch. DEC is absent from inspected master/dev and remains in inspected staging. This change does not establish removal from older tagged releases. The setup wizard no longer automatically recommends this branch-dependent setting.

features.name: Quiet Mode
features.officialDefinition: Suppresses non-critical audio alerts and chimes while driving. sunnypilot will only sound alarms for situations requiring immediate driver attention, keeping visual feedback active while eliminating routine cabin beeps.
features.userSummary: Silences non-critical chimes while preserving safety alarms.
features.userTranslation: "Silent Cruising." Turns off routine beeps and chimes so you can enjoy quiet music or conversations, but will still sound loud emergency alarms if you need to take over immediately.

features.name: ICBM
features.officialDefinition: A system designed to manage vehicle speed by electronically "pressing" the car's native cruise control buttons (RES+/SET-) to mimic full longitudinal control on cars that do not support it natively.
features.userSummary: Allows smart speed control on unsupported cars by simulating button presses.
features.userTranslation: "Cruise Hacker." If your car doesn't support full self-driving gas/brake, this feature simulates your steering wheel buttons to force the car to slow down for curves or speed limits. SCC-L is a proposed extension in issue #1846 to use model longitudinal output as an ICBM speed-target source. It is not an available SCC-V/SCC-M option.

features.name: SCC-V
features.officialDefinition: Smart Cruise Control - Vision (SCC-V) leverages camera vision data to proactively adjust your vehicle’s speed by calculating curvature in the road ahead.
features.userSummary: Slows down for curves it sees with the camera.
features.userTranslation: "Eyes-On Curve Slowdown." The car sees a sharp turn coming and smoothly slows down before entering the curve, just like a human driver would.

features.name: SCC-M
features.officialDefinition: Uses OpenStreetMap (OSM) data to anticipate upcoming road curvature and lower the ACC set speed accordingly using jerk-based distance planning.
features.userSummary: Slows down for curves using map data.
features.userTranslation: "Map-Based Curve Slowdown." The car looks at the map, sees a curve ahead, and slows down before you can even see it.

features.name: SLA
features.officialDefinition: Reads speed limits from vehicle-provided sign data and downloaded maps. Off, Information, Warning, and Assist modes control how the limit is shown or used; cruise-speed adjustment depends on longitudinal control or ICBM and confirmation rules.
features.userSummary: Displays or warns about limits; Assist can manage cruise speed on compatible configurations.
features.userTranslation: Assist is not an unconditional automatic SET mode. Speed-limit changes may require cruise-button confirmation, depending on vehicle configuration and speed. PR #2042 proposes a separate opt-in map-based Auto SET mode limited to Honda City 7G with openpilot longitudinal and non-PCM cruise. It is open and unmerged; physical instrument-cluster validation is pending. Source: https://github.com/sunnypilot/sunnypilot/pull/2042

features.name: Custom ACC
features.officialDefinition: Allows configuration of the speed increment/decrement values for Short Press (e.g., ±1) and Long Press (e.g., ±5) of the cruise buttons.
features.userSummary: Remap cruise button speed increment values.
features.userTranslation: "Button Step Sizer." Customize your steering wheel buttons so one tap changes speed by 1 mph and holding it jumps by 5 mph (or any step size you choose).

features.name: Alpha Longitudinal
features.officialDefinition: sunnypilot's custom in-house longitudinal control implementation. Delivers refined acceleration smoothing, stopped-car creeping, and improved stop-and-go behavior over stock OEM cruise.
features.userSummary: sunnypilot's custom gas and brake control algorithm.
features.userTranslation: "Custom Gas & Brake." Replaces your car's factory radar cruise control with sunnypilot's own throttle and braking logic, allowing for smoother slowdowns and custom car following distances.

features.name: ALC
features.officialDefinition: Initiates a lane change after a blinker input and a configurable delay timer, without requiring a torque "nudge" on the steering wheel. Integrates with Blind Spot Monitoring (BSM) for safety.
features.userSummary: Tap blinker -> Car moves over automatically after safe check.
features.userTranslation: "Hands-Free Lane Change." You flick the turn signal, sunnypilot verifies the blind spot is clear, waits your preferred delay timer, and executes a smooth lane change automatically.

features.name: OSM Maps
features.officialDefinition: Integrates downloaded OpenStreetMap (OSM) vector data onto the device. Provides offline road geometry, curve curvature, and verified speed limits without requiring mobile cellular coverage during your drives.
features.userSummary: Offline maps powering curve slowing and speed limits.
features.userTranslation: "Offline Road Knowledge." Downloads maps directly to your device storage so sunnypilot knows speed limits and sharp upcoming curves even when driving through remote areas with zero cell signal.

features.name: HUD & Visuals
features.officialDefinition: A suite of driving screen HUD overlays including real-time acceleration (Rocket Fuel Bar), lead vehicle distance and speed metrics below the chevron, standstill timers, true speedometer readings, and blind spot warning visuals.
features.userSummary: Custom driving screen telemetry, acceleration bar, and lead car stats.
features.userTranslation: "Pro HUD Dash." Enhances your screen with rich telemetry: see the exact distance and speed of the car ahead, a color-coded G-force acceleration bar, and how long you have been stopped at a red light.

features.name: Models & AI
features.officialDefinition: Allows switching and testing different vision neural network driving models directly on device. Configure advanced model parameters including lane turn desires, live learning steer delay, and camera software delay.
features.userSummary: In-cab AI model switcher with fine-tuning parameters.
features.userTranslation: Inspected master, dev and staging now use selector 21, Chestnut v28 and Qualcomm v25, with Mountain Dew Model v3 as the default big model. Older builds use different catalogs. Check hardware and branch compatibility; refresh while parked with no download running. Clear Cache removes downloaded models.

features.name: sunnylink
features.officialDefinition: sunnypilot's cloud backend system connecting your device to the web management dashboard. Enables automated configuration backup and restore, GitHub sponsorship synchronization, and remote parameter toggling.
features.userSummary: Cloud backup, web dashboard, and remote parameter management.
features.userTranslation: "Cloud Companion." Connects your device to sunnylink.ai so you can backup your settings, tune parameters from your phone, and link your GitHub account for sponsor features.

features.name: HKG Tuning
features.officialDefinition: Applies specific tuning profiles ("Stock" or "Dynamic") to the longitudinal control policy for Hyundai/Kia/Genesis (HKG) vehicles. Integrates with native Highway Driving Assist (HDA) status.
features.userSummary: Gas pedal responsiveness for Hyundai/Kia/Genesis.
features.userTranslation: "Hyundai Gas Pedal Fix." If your Kia/Hyundai accelerates too slowly or feels sluggish when resuming from stops, switching this to "Dynamic" improves throttle response.

features.name: Speed-Dependent Steering Delay (Open PR)
features.officialDefinition: PR #2029 proposes speed-dependent fixed steering delay when live learning is disabled: a city boost blends down to the highway delay.
features.userSummary: Development proposal: improve low-speed turns without excessive highway delay.
features.userTranslation: City Delay Boost is proposed under Models. It applies only with live steering-delay learning off. It is not confirmed in a stable release.

features.name: Smooth Final Stop Braking (Draft)
features.officialDefinition: Draft PR #2034 adjusts the longitudinal controller stopping transition to reduce abrupt braking at the final stop.
features.userSummary: Draft controller improvement for a softer final stop.
features.userTranslation: Applies when sunnypilot controls acceleration and braking. No independent toggle is documented, and stock ACC does not gain this behavior from a wiki setting.

features.name: Chestnut Runtime & Power (Development)
features.officialDefinition: Chestnut GPU models are already catalogued. Open PR #2035 proposes resizing comma 3X frames to 1344×760 before unified AMD-model transfer; open PR #2023 proposes a GPU power limit adjustable through sunnylink.
features.userSummary: Development updates for comma 3X frame transfer and Chestnut power management.
features.userTranslation: Resizing reduces camera transfer bandwidth; it requires the relevant runtime branch and compatible Chestnut hardware. The proposed power limit is 0 for stock or 40–100 W, exposed through advanced sunnylink Device settings for comma four.

features.name: Model Runtime Startup Troubleshooting
features.officialDefinition: PR #1999 proposed changes for a misleading Posenet NaN-speed alert during compiled-model startup, but was closed without merging on October 16, 2026.
features.userSummary: An initialization failure can appear as a Posenet speed error.
features.userTranslation: Do not treat PR #1999 as an available fix. Persistent alerts still require runtime diagnostics; clearing the model cache alone does not establish a repaired runtime.

features.name: Third-Party Authentication (Requested)
features.officialDefinition: Issue #1857 requests an OIDC device authorization grant or Home Assistant OAuth redirect for user-authorized sunnylink API integrations.
features.userSummary: Requested authentication flow for Home Assistant and other integrations.
features.userTranslation: Neither requested flow is documented as enabled. Device credentials and user OAuth tokens serve different roles. Follow the issue for supported authorization before attempting integration setup.

features.name: Software Update Troubleshooting
features.officialDefinition: Open issue #2020 reports that ignition before Install Now is tapped can discard an already-prepared OTA update.
features.userSummary: Install prepared updates while parked before starting ignition.
features.userTranslation: Allow installation and reboot to complete before ignition. If Install Now disappears, return offroad with unmetered Wi-Fi and allow the updater to fetch and prepare again. Metered recovery may be delayed by up to three days according to the report.

features.name: Jetlink (Closed Proposal)
features.officialDefinition: PR #2001 proposed external NVIDIA Jetson acceleration over USB for large driving models and was closed without merging.
features.userSummary: Experimental Jetson offload proposal; not an upstream released feature.
features.userTranslation: The proposal used a separate ONNX catalog and TensorRT preparation while parked, with a local small model during startup or recovery. Existing QCOM model bundles are not TensorRT inputs. The closed PR does not establish supported availability.

features.name: 2026.003.000 Development Milestone
features.officialDefinition: Milestone #6 includes open PR #1741 for a configurable low-voltage shutdown threshold and open PR #1767 for a detailed comma four (MICI) onroad view.
features.userSummary: Planned power and display work remains under review.
features.userTranslation: Check your build and the individual PRs. The milestone is open and does not mean these changes have shipped in all staging or release branches.

features.name: HKG Dynamic Steering Torque (Requested)
features.officialDefinition: Open issue #1052 proposes dynamically inferring steering torque limits for Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis instead of relying only on fixed platform tables.
features.userSummary: Proposed adaptive EPS torque limits; not an available setting.
features.userTranslation: This remains a feature request. It does not authorize overriding vehicle safety limits or imply automatic EPS-limit discovery in released builds.

features.name: SCC-L (Requested)
features.officialDefinition: Open issue #1846 proposes using model longitudinal output as an ICBM cruise-speed target source.
features.userSummary: Request to extend ICBM with longitudinal model cues.
features.userTranslation: Existing ICBM and SCC-V/SCC-M documentation still applies. SCC-L has no confirmed implementation or parameter to enable.

glossary.ACC: Adaptive Cruise Control - Maintains set speed and follows traffic
glossary.ALC: Automatic Lane Centering / Automatic Lane Change - Keeps car centered or changes lanes automatically
glossary.BSM: Blind Spot Monitoring - Vehicle sensors detecting cars in adjacent lanes
glossary.DEC: Dynamic Experimental Control — legacy mode switching; removed from current master/dev, retained in inspected staging.
glossary.E2E: End-to-End - AI neural network that directly predicts vehicle driving path
glossary.ESCC: Enhanced Smart Cruise Control - Hyundai/Kia cruise management and button integration
glossary.Firehose: Large-scale automated driving telemetry upload system contributing to driving model training
glossary.HDA: Highway Driving Assist - Hyundai/Kia native factory highway system
glossary.HKG: Hyundai/Kia/Genesis - South Korean automotive platform family
glossary.ICBM: Intelligent Cruise Button Management - Electronically manages steering wheel cruise buttons
glossary.LDW: Lane Departure Warning - Visual/haptic warnings when drifting out of lane
glossary.MADS: Modular Assistive Driving System - sunnypilot exclusive decoupled steering and cruise architecture
glossary.MICI: comma four hardware platform code designation
glossary.NNLC: Neural Network Lateral Control - Deep learning model predicting steering trajectories
glossary.OSM: OpenStreetMap - Open-source global map database used for offline curvature and speed limits
glossary.PID: Proportional-Integral-Derivative - Classic mathematical feedback controller for steering
glossary.SDSU: Smart DSU - Aftermarket hardware interceptor for older Toyota radar cruise support
glossary.SLA: Speed Limit Assist - Automatic cruise set-speed adjustment based on legal road limits
glossary.SCC-M: Smart Cruise Control Map - Curve speed reduction based on OSM map geometry
glossary.SCC-V: Smart Cruise Control Vision - Curve speed reduction based on front camera perception
glossary.TSR: Traffic Sign Recognition - Camera-based detection of road speed limit signs
glossary.UEM: Unified Engagement Mode - Single button engagement option for MADS
glossary.WMI: World Model Iteration - Advanced E2E model architecture
glossary.ZSS: Zorro Steering Sensor - High-resolution optical steering angle sensor for older Toyotas
